title: machine stop leaves server9p + gvproxy orphaned (Hyper-V), next start fails
body:
### Issue Description

On Windows/Hyper-V, a clean `podman machine stop` (exit 0, VM off) leaves both helper daemons running: `podman machine server9p --serve ...` and `gvproxy`. The next `podman machine start` then fails, and the orphaned server9p keeps whatever state it held (in our case 11M+ leaked handles).

This differs from #29474 (orphans after killing the VM from another client like `wsl --shutdown` or `Stop-VM`): here no external kill happens — the plain stop path itself doesn't reap its own sidecars. Related: #30134 (same server9p process leaking ~8 handles per 9p file op); an orphaned server keeps that leaked kernel memory alive indefinitely.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Windows 11, `podman machine init --provider hyperv` + `podman machine start` (8 CPU / 2 GiB).
2. Run any workload with 9p file traffic (e.g. create+read a few thousand small files under a 9p bind), then `podman machine stop` (exits 0, VM reports off).
3. `Get-Process podman,gvproxy` — both `server9p --serve ...` and `gvproxy` are still alive (server9p keeps its full handle count).
4. `podman machine start` fails with: `could not start api proxy since expected pipe is not available` (plus ssh-port conflict warnings on the first retry).
5. Manual `taskkill /PID <both>` + `podman machine start` = green.

### Describe the results you received

Clean stop leaves orphans behind; next start fails until the orphans are killed by hand. The orphaned server9p also preserves its leaked handle table across the stop (11M handles still held with the VM off).

### Describe the results you expected

`machine stop` reaps the sidecars it started (or start tolerates/replaces them): after a successful stop, no `server9p`/`gvproxy` tied to that machine should remain.

(Full 160-line `podman info` on file; trimmed to the identifying fields. Complete output available on request.)

### Podman in a container

No

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (build 26200), Hyper-V provider, machine 8 CPU / 2 GiB / 100 GiB, default 9p shares, no Podman Desktop involved.

### Additional information

The orphans survive every clean stop (reproduced 2/2, plus one stale-gvproxy block of a later start fixed the same way). I did not test `machine rm` cleanup. Workaround today: kill both PIDs by hand and retry start — which is also how the reporter of #29474 recovered, but that issue's trigger (external VM kill) does not apply here.
